title: Navigating the Sparse Landscape of Men's Mental Health Support
excerpt: In the realm of mental health, men often find themselves navigating a path that is under-recognized and sparsely resourced. Despite growing awareness, the stark reality remains...
content:
In the realm of mental health, men often find themselves navigating a path that is under-recognized and sparsely resourced. Despite growing awareness, the stark reality remains: there are few places where men can truly feel comfortable seeking and receiving the help they need. Today, we're addressing this gap, acknowledging the hurdles, and offering a hand of support to those who may be silently struggling.

The pressures of masculinity can create an isolating experience for many men living with mental health issues. Society's expectations often dictate a narrative of self-reliance and stoicism, leaving little room for vulnerability. As a result, many men endure in silence, fearing judgment or misunderstanding should they express their emotional struggles.

This silence can be deafening and, for many, detrimental. The statistics are sobering, with men accounting for a high percentage of deaths by suicide, yet they are less likely to access psychological therapies compared to their female counterparts. This discrepancy highlights a clear need for more gender-specific support systems that cater to the unique ways in which men communicate and experience mental health challenges.

So, where does one turn when the avenues of support seem so narrow? The answer, while not simple, begins with a single step: reaching out. To extend a hand for help is perhaps the hardest hurdle to overcome, but it is also the most critical. We are here to grasp that hand firmly and pull together.

Support comes in many forms: a listening ear, a shared experience, or professional guidance. It's vital to create spaces where men can speak openly, without fear of judgment or stigma. A conversation with a trusted friend, a support group with others who understand, a therapy session with a trained professional - these are lifelines that can lead to recovery and resilience.

We are here to bridge the gap, to stand in the sparse spaces of men's mental health support and fill them with understanding and assistance. Whether it's through community groups, helplines, or mental health services, the goal is to ensure that every man knows he does not have to walk this path alone.

If you or someone you know is facing mental health challenges, we implore you to reach out. Our communities need fathers, brothers, sons, and friends to stand tall - not in solitude, but in solidarity. Let's dismantle the barriers, one conversation at a time, and build a network of support for every man who needs it.

Remember, the strength to reach out and accept help is not just a personal triumph, but a beacon of hope for others who may be lost in the silence. Together, we can create a chorus of support loud enough to be heard by every man who needs to hear it:

You are not alone, and help is here.

title: Understanding and Navigating Men's Mental Health Challenges in Geelong
excerpt: Understanding and Navigating Men's Mental Health Challenges in Geelong, Victoria Welcome, while Men’s Mental Health has been hidden from the public eye, it is of paramount...
content:
Understanding and Navigating Men's Mental Health Challenges in Geelong, Victoria

Welcome, while Men’s Mental Health has been hidden from the public eye, it is of paramount importance to the well-being of our community. In Geelong, Victoria, we're striving to bring this issue to light and provide support where it's needed most. Men’s mental health is an often-overlooked aspect of our societal well-being, yet it is equally as important as any other facet of healthcare. In Geelong, the challenges that men face can be as diverse as the population itself, ranging from stress and anxiety related to employment or financial pressures, to more severe mental health conditions such as depression and PTSD. While societal norms have traditionally dictated a stoic demeanour among men, it's crucial to understand that vulnerability is not a sign of weakness, but rather an aspect of the human condition. In our community, we're working to shift the paradigm, encouraging men to speak openly about their mental health and seek support without stigma or judgment. Monthly Meetings: A Space for Support and Connection To provide a safe and welcoming environment, we've established a monthly gathering that offers men in Geelong the opportunity to come together. This initiative is not just a meeting; it’s a sanctuary where honesty is met with understanding and compassion. Each month, we invite guest speakers who share their expertise and personal experiences relating to mental health. We believe that through education and shared narratives, we can dismantle the barriers that keep men from seeking help. After our discussions, we bond over a casual barbecue, an Australian tradition that fosters camaraderie and comfort. It’s during these moments that conversations often transcend the superficial, touching on deeper, more personal experiences. It is here, among peers and the aroma of a sizzling barbie, that walls come down and true healing can begin. Mental Health Agencies: The Support Networks Available For those in need of professional support, Geelong is home to a number of mental health agencies dedicated to assisting men through difficult times. Below are some of the resources available to our community:

  • Headspace Geelong - Catering specifically to youth, headspace provides early intervention mental health services for 12 to 25-year-old
  • Beyond Blue - Offering comprehensive support for Australians experiencing anxiety, depression, or suicide ideation, Beyond Blue is a national name with local services, including in Geelong.
  • Lifeline Geelong - Lifeline offers 24-hour crisis support and suicide prevention services, ensuring that help is available at any time, day or night.
  • MensLine Australia - A dedicated service for men with relationship, family, or well-being concerns.
  • Barwon Health - Through Barwon Health, locals can access a range of mental health services, including counselling and therapy.
These organizations play a critical role in our support network, and we encourage anyone who is struggling to reach out to them. Remember, reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. In conclusion, the journey toward better mental health is a collective one. In Geelong, we pledge to walk alongside our brothers, fathers, sons, and friends, offering a hand when the road gets tough. Our monthly meetings are just the beginning. Together, we can create a future where no man needs to walk alone in the face of mental health challenges. If you, or someone you know, is in need of support, please contact one of the organizations listed above or join us at our next monthly meeting.

title: International Men's Day 2023
excerpt: The day serves as an important catalyst for drawing attention to the specific health and well-being challenges that affect the male populace. In the current year, the spotlight is...
content:
The day serves as an important catalyst for drawing attention to the specific health and well-being challenges that affect the male populace. In the current year, the spotlight is cast on the critical issues of
  • suicide
  • mental health
Acknowledging the alarming statistic that males are disproportionately more likely to die by suicide in comparison to their female counterparts. The prevalence of mental health disorders does not discriminate between genders; however, the manifestation and handling of these conditions often diverge significantly between men and women.

Dissecting the Mental Health Gender Disparity

The issue of the mental health gender gap is nuanced and resists oversimplification. Nonetheless, clinical observations frequently point to distinct patterns in the way men and women present with and communicate their psychological distress.

Catalysts and Presentation of Symptoms

Among men, the principal catalysts for onset of depression and anxiety are frequently linked to
  • occupational stress
  • financial duress
  • interpersonal relationship strife
With respect to depression, there is a noted propensity for males to exhibit less of the conventional indicators such as persistent sadness or crying. They are more likely to display symptoms that may include irritability, displays of anger, and a predilection for risk-taking behaviours. Regarding anxiety, males often report somatic symptoms such as muscular tension, gastrointestinal distress, and cephalgia, among others. In contrast, females typically articulate emotional symptoms, including pervasive worry, apprehension, and agitation.

Stigma in Society and Communicative Expressions

Cultural norms from a young age may instil in males a sense of stoicism and self-reliance, coupled with a propensity to conceal their emotional state. Consequently, men may be more reticent to disclose mental health concerns due to apprehensions about perceived weakness. Women, conversely, often find it more permissible to vocalize their emotions and seek support.

Coping Strategies and Suicidality

Females generally tend to seek out social sustenance and verbalize their emotions, while males may prefer to engage in physical or task-oriented coping mechanisms. Males are also more susceptible to resort to substance misuse, particularly alcohol, social withdrawal, and other deleterious behaviours. The reluctance to seek assistance for psychological issues contributes to the distressing reality that men are approximately three times more likely to die by suicide. In the year 2022 the latest available statistics show, the male demographic constituted 75.6% of suicide mortalities, with the median age being 46 years.

Strategies to Enhance Men’s Mental Health Support

To make improvements to mental health outcomes for men necessitates cultivating an inclusive and empathetic milieu. Strategies to bolster support for men include:
  • Fostering Open Dialogue Cultivating an empathetic setting where men are comfortable to speak candidly about their mental health tribulations is imperative.
  • Loved ones can play an integral role in facilitating non-judgmental dialogue. It is imperative to recognize that no concern is too trivial. Unaddressed issues can escalate if not confronted promptly.
  • Advocating for Professional Intervention Healthcare professionals can offer customized support to meet the unique mental health requirements of men.
  • Referrals to a general practitioner or the Australian Psychological Society can facilitate connections with appropriate psychological services.
  • Male-Centric Support Networks Support groups tailored to males can provide a secure environment for sharing experiences and overcoming societal stigma..
  • Workplace Initiatives Employers are positioned to significantly influence men's mental health through employee assistance programs (EAPs), flexible employment arrangements, and mental health education. A supportive workplace culture is fundamental.
  • Community Participation Engagement in community endeavours can foster social ties and mitigate feelings of isolation. Active involvement in sports, hobbies, and volunteer work can be instrumental in building connections.
Organizations like Relationships Australia and ManOnline offer a safe and accepting space for connection. Online resources such as MensLine Australia and Head to Health also offer valuable support. International Men's Day not only celebrates men's contributions to life and society but also emphasizes the distinctive mental health hurdles they face. Understanding the differences in mental health expression and help-seeking behaviours between genders is critical. By creating an environment where men are encouraged to communicate their mental health challenges and seek professional assistance, we can make substantial progress in improving mental well-being for all men.

title: How We Are Creating a Supportive Environment at The Wandering Man
excerpt: Creating a supportive environment for men’s mental health involves a multi-faceted approach, both in personal spaces such as the home or workplace, and in wider community...
content:
Creating a supportive environment for men’s mental health involves a multi-faceted approach, both in personal spaces such as the home or workplace, and in wider community settings. Here are several strategies to foster such an environment:
  1. Promote Open Dialogue: Encourage conversations about mental health that challenge stereotypes and stigma. Facilitating workshops or training sessions that focus on the importance of mental health can help normalize these discussions.
  2. Educate and Raise Awareness: Create awareness campaigns that specifically target men’s mental health issues. Use media, literature, and events to educate the public and dismantle myths about masculinity and mental health.
  3. Train Staff: In the workplace, ensure that human resources staff and managers are trained to recognize signs of mental distress and are knowledgeable about how to respond appropriately.
  4. Provide Resources: Offer access to mental health resources such as counseling services, employee assistance programs (EAPs), and self-help materials. Providing a list of helplines, websites, and local services can also be valuable.
  5. Develop Support Networks: Establish support groups or peer networks where men can share experiences and coping strategies in a safe and confidential space.
  6. Encourage Work-Life Balance: Promote policies that support a healthy work-life balance, such as flexible working hours, parental leave, and time off for mental health.
  7. Lead by Example: Leaders and role models should speak openly about their own experiences with mental health to set a precedent that it is okay to seek help.
  8. Destigmatize Help-Seeking: Counteract the stigma associated with psychological therapy or counseling by normalizing these services as a routine part of health care.
  9. Accessible Mental Health Services: Ensure that mental health services are accessible, which may involve offering services outside of traditional work hours, providing online or telehealth options, and considering the financial accessibility of such services.
  10. Tailor Approaches to Men: Develop and offer programs that are designed with the unique ways men communicate and seek support in mind. These might include activity-based therapy or approaches that focus on problem-solving.
  11. Ensure Confidentiality: Assure individuals that their privacy will be respected when they seek help, which is often a concern that prevents men from reaching out.
  12. Foster Community Involvement: Engage community leaders, sports clubs, and other groups in mental health initiatives to reach men in different contexts.
Ultimately, a supportive environment for men's mental health is one that acknowledges the unique pressures men may face, provides multiple avenues for support, and respects individual experiences and coping mechanisms. It should always be reinforced that seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness.

Our Grand Prix Meeting and BBQ Announcement

We're thrilled to share some exciting news with our readers this month! We have the honor of hosting two distinguished speakers who are set to inspire and enlighten us with their experiences and insights. Firstly, we welcome Scott West, an icon of the Australian Football League and a name synonymous with the Footscray Western Bulldogs. Scott's football career is nothing short of legendary; he's a player who has not only been inducted into the AFL Hall of Fame in 2013 but has also earned the Charlie Sutton Medal a record seven times. His reputation as one of the Bulldogs' all-time greats is well-deserved. Known for his tenacious midfield play, particularly in tight contests and stoppages, Scott consistently ranked among the top for possessions in the league. We're eager to hear about the drive and determination that propelled him to such heights in his sporting career. In addition to Scott's athletic prowess, we are privileged to have Shannon Bowman join us. Shannon is the visionary behind Create Balance Psychotherapy and Counselling, based right here in Geelong. As an accredited Mental Health and Social Worker (AMHSW) and an accredited EMDR Practitioner, Shannon brings a wealth of experience to the table. He is passionate about people's ability to change and grow, and he's dedicated his career to guiding individuals on their personal journeys toward healing and self-improvement. Shannon's expert insights into mental health and well-being are sure to be a highlight for all who attend. Mark your calendars and prepare to be inspired by these two remarkable individuals who are making a difference in their respective fields. Stay tuned for more details on this not-to-be-missed event!

title: Tying Our Mission Statement, Values and Two Pillar Strategy Together
excerpt: Tying Our Mission Statement, Values, and Two Pillar Strategy Together At the heart of our men’s mental health group lies a mission that is both ambitious and compassionate: to...
content:
Tying Our Mission Statement, Values, and Two Pillar Strategy Together 

At the heart of our men’s mental health group lies a mission that is both ambitious and compassionate: to create an inclusive community where empathy, respect, and confidentiality are not just words, but the bedrock of our day-to-day interactions. Our commitment to this mission is unwavering, as is our dedication to the values and pillars that support it. Here’s how our mission statement, values, and three pillars are intricately woven to form the fabric of our organization.  Mission Statement: A Beacon of Brotherhood  Our mission statement serves as a guiding beacon, illuminating the path we walk together in support of men’s mental health. We envision a world where no man is left to face his mental health struggles alone. Through fostering an inclusive community built on understanding and mutual support, we help individuals not just to endure but to thrive. Each word in our mission is a promise to uphold the integrity of our purpose and to ensure that every man’s journey is met with the understanding and support needed for personal growth and resilience.  Our Values: The Moral Compass  Integrity, empathy, respect, confidentiality, and empowerment are the core values that serve as our moral compass. Each value is interdependent, informing and reinforcing the other: 
  • Integrity ensures that trust is never compromised. It allows our members to feel safe, knowing that their voices will be heard in a space where honesty is paramount. 
  • Empathy is the heart of connection, allowing us to truly understand and support one another. It is through empathy that our messages of hope are felt deeply and personal experiences are shared openly. 
  • Respect assures each individual that their story is important and that their voice is an essential contribution to the chorus of our community. 
  • Confidentiality is the shield that protects our members, giving them the confidence to share without fear of judgment or exposure. 
  • Empowerment is the result of our collective efforts, equipping each member with the courage and resources to take control of their mental health journey. 
Our Three Pillars Strategy: The Framework of Our Community  The three pillars of Education, Collaboration, and Brotherhood are the framework upon which our community is built: 
  • Education is the pillar that enlightens and informs, turning the darkness of ignorance into the light of understanding and acceptance. We continually strive to provide a wealth of resources and learning opportunities, encouraging members to become students and teachers in their own right. 
  • Collaboration is the pillar that unites us, ensuring that every member knows they are not alone. It’s in our meetings, workshops, and shared stories that the strength of our bonds is forged, turning individual struggles into collective triumphs. 
  • Brotherhood is the final pillar, the ultimate goal of our mission. It’s in the sense of brotherhood that we find the durability to withstand any storm. Here, each member is not just part of a group but a vital piece of a larger family. 
A Unified Vision  By living our values and upholding our pillars, we fulfill our mission. Each element complements the other, creating a holistic approach to men’s mental health that is dynamic and robust. Our mission statement is our destination, our values are the compass that guides us, and our pillars are the strong foundation upon which we stand. Together, they create a sanctuary where transformative experiences lead to a stronger, more resilient sense of brotherhood - one where no man is left behind.

title: Advice for Adults - Responding to Bullying of Youths
excerpt: Offer support and reassurance; make it clear to the youth that they are not alone and are in a safe space. Request that the leader or supervisor of the environment where the...
content:
Offer support and reassurance; make it clear to the youth that they are not alone and are in a safe space.
Request that the leader or supervisor of the environment where the bullying occurs keep a watchful eye on the interactions there.
Ensure the safety of the bullied individual by arranging for adult supervision or the presence of a responsible older youth in the vicinity of the bullying.
Aid in fostering self-confidence, enhancing self-worth, and promoting open communication.

ADVICE FOR ADULTS - WHEN A BULLYING VICTIM EXPRESSES SUICIDAL IDEATION

Address the issue head-on by asking the individual if they have thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
In the case of an affirmative response, do not delay in seeking professional assistance. Contact a local support or crisis center to get the necessary help.
Should the individual disclose a specific plan for suicide, immediately call emergency services by dialling 000 (or the appropriate emergency number for your country).

GUIDANCE FOR YOUTHS OBSERVING OR EXPERIENCING BULLYING

When witnessing bullying, assess the situation to determine the safest way to intervene. You might directly tell the aggressor to stop, provide support to the victim, and/or seek assistance from an adult.
If you are the target of bullying, assert yourself by maintaining a poised demeanour, making steady eye contact, and speaking in a firm yet calm voice. Command the bully to cease their behaviours and then remove yourself from the situation. Always reach out to an adult and do not keep the experience of bullying to yourself.

title: Breaking the Silence About the Mental Health Crisis Among Men
excerpt: In our ongoing conversation about the importance of mental health, we come across statistics that are more than mere numbers; they are stark indicators of a crisis that needs...
content:
In our ongoing conversation about the importance of mental health, we come across statistics that are more than mere numbers; they are stark indicators of a crisis that needs immediate attention and collective action. The latest data from the Australia Bureau of Statistics' Causes of Death, released in 2022, casts a spotlight on a particularly vulnerable segment of our society: men and their mental health struggles.

The findings are sobering. Men are tragically three times more likely to die by suicide than women. In 2022, an overwhelming 75.6% of suicide deaths were men - that's 2,455 lives lost.

When we look closer, we see that the median age of these men was 46 years, an age that should be in the prime of life. Yet, for many, it is a time of overwhelming struggle that, for some, ends in suicide.

This isn't just a statistic; it's a community of fathers, sons, brothers, and friends. The age-standardized suicide rate among men increased marginally but significantly, from 18.3 to 18.8 per 100,000 population from 2021 to 2022. Suicide ranks as the 11th leading cause of death for males and, even more distressingly, as the highest-ranked external cause of death.

Men aged 45-49 are facing the starkest reality, with the highest suicide rates among those under 80. Over 10% of male suicides were in this age group, which saw the largest increase in their age-specific suicide rate. This paints a picture of a crisis that cannot be ignored.

Risk factors are key to understanding and prevention. The data shows that nearly 86% of suicide deaths involved at least one identified risk factor, with psychosocial troubles topping the list. Among the most common were mood disorders, thoughts of suicide, and spousal relationship problems.

For men aged 25-44, relationship issues became the most prevalent risk factor, overtaking mood disorders for the first time.

For women, mood disorders were the leading risk factor, followed by a personal history of self-harm and suicide ideation. The gender-specific nature of these risk factors underscores the need for a responsive and sensitive approach to mental health support that caters to the unique experiences of both men and women.

Our blog is more than a platform for discussion; it's a call to action. These statistics represent real people in our communities who are suffering in silence.

We must shine a light on mental health and break the stigma that prevents so many from seeking help. It's time to advocate for comprehensive mental health education, accessible care, and a society that nurtures rather than neglects the emotional well-being of all its members.

Together, we can make a difference and change the narrative around mental health, one post at a time.

title: Mindful Social - Cultivating Mental Wellness Through Positive Online Connections
excerpt: As a mental health expert, I have seen firsthand the impact that social media can have on an individual's mental wellness. The networks we build through these platforms can either...
content:
As a mental health expert, I have seen firsthand the impact that social media can have on an individual's mental wellness. The networks we build through these platforms can either enhance our optimism, positive self-image, and connectedness, or they can contribute to feelings of loneliness, inadequacy, and even exacerbate mental health disorders.

It is crucial to curate our social media spaces in a way that promotes positive mental health. By following hashtags and accounts that motivate and ground us, we can create a feed that uplifts and inspires us. Engaging with posts that are rooted in gratitude and celebration can have a contagious effect, spreading positivity to our own emotions.

Research has shown that emotions expressed by others on social media can influence our own, so it is important to be mindful of the content we consume and share.

Utilizing social media as a creative outlet for self-expression can also be beneficial for our mental wellness.

It is essential to prioritize real connections and relationships on social media, rather than engaging in voyeurism that can lead to feelings of loneliness and inadequacy. Remember that social media should enhance, not replace, offline activities and social connections.

Being analytical and selective about the information we consume and share is crucial for maintaining our mental wellness. Conducting a privacy checkup on our social media platforms can also help us be aware of what information is being shared with whom and protect our online privacy.

By following these tips for positive social media use, we can cultivate a space that enhances our mental wellness, strengthens our connections, and potentially acts as a protective factor against mental health disorders. Remember, your mental health is important, and it is okay to set boundaries and curate your online spaces to prioritize your well-being.

title: Australia is facing an urgent need for mental health reform
excerpt: Australia is facing an urgent need for mental health reform. The rate of young people experiencing mental health conditions has significantly increased over the years, from 25% in...
content:
Australia is facing an urgent need for mental health reform. The rate of young people experiencing mental health conditions has significantly increased over the years, from 25% in 2007 to 40% in 2021. Mental health issues have become the most common reason for people to seek help from general practitioners (GPs), and it is a growing concern for GPs in the future.

However, despite the alarming increase in mental health conditions, the investment in mental health is inadequate. Mental health expenditure as a proportion of total health expenditure has actually decreased from 8% in 2019-20 to 7% in 2020-21. This is well below the recommended 13% proportion based on the burden of disease. The Productivity Commission has recommended an additional $1.2 billion per year investment from governments to implement priority mental health system reforms.

The current cost of living crisis is adding further strain to people's mental health. A report by Mental Health Australia found that 1 in 2 people in Australia believe that the rising cost of living is significantly impacting their mental health, and 1 in 5 individuals see cost as a barrier to accessing mental health support. Out-of-pocket healthcare fees are also increasing, making it harder for individuals to seek mental health support and exacerbating health inequalities.

While the Australian Government has made some progress in mental health reform, such as investing in new peak bodies and improving access to mental health support, there is still more work to be done. The government needs to collaborate with the mental health sector, individuals with lived experience, and their families and carers to bring about fundamental reforms to the mental health system. This includes responding to evaluations and reviews, implementing workforce strategies, and integrating mental health into the national health reform agreement.

Investing in mental health will not only result in improved quality of life for individuals but also lead to cost savings and increased economic productivity.

By investing in mental health, the government can also progress towards a healthier, more secure, sustainable, cohesive, and prosperous Australia.

title: Strategies for Finding Peace and Wellbeing in Our Busy Lives
excerpt: Stress is a natural response to challenges in our lives, and in small amounts, it can even be helpful. However, prolonged periods of stress can have negative effects on our...
content:
Stress is a natural response to challenges in our lives, and in small amounts, it can even be helpful. However, prolonged periods of stress can have negative effects on our physical and mental well-being, particularly in our busy lives. This document aims to provide an understanding of stress, its symptoms, and effective strategies to alleviate stress and promote a sense of peace.

We will explore what stress is and how it affects us, recognizing that everyone experiences and responds to stress differently. We will identify common signs and symptoms of harmful stress, such as headaches, disturbed sleeping patterns, fatigue, and changes in appetite. Understanding these symptoms can help us take proactive steps towards managing stress effectively.

To alleviate stress, we will delve into nine powerful strategies that can make a profound difference in our lives. These strategies include practicing stress-management techniques, engaging in regular physical activity or exercise, prioritizing self-care activities, seeking social support, managing time effectively, setting boundaries, taking breaks, challenging negative thoughts, and seeking professional help if necessary.

By implementing these strategies, we can navigate through our busy lives with greater ease and find a sense of peace amidst the challenges. Remember, stress management is a lifelong journey, and prioritizing our mental and emotional well-being is essential for a healthy and fulfilling life.

I would conclude that stress is a natural response to challenges and can be helpful in small amounts. However, prolonged periods of stress can have negative effects on our physical and mental wellbeing. It is important to be aware of the symptoms of harmful stress, which can include headaches, disturbed sleeping patterns, fatigue, upset stomach, muscle tension, high blood pressure, weakened immune system, feeling overwhelmed or out of control, feeling anxious or worried, difficulty concentrating, lack of motivation, and changes in appetite. To alleviate stress in our busy lives, some strategies that can make a profound difference include:

  1. Practice stress-management techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, or mindfulness: These techniques help to calm the mind, reduce anxiety, and promote relaxation. Deep breathing involves taking slow, deep breaths to activate the body's relaxation response. Meditation and mindfulness involve focusing on the present moment and cultivating a sense of awareness and acceptance.
  2. Engage in regular physical activity or exercise: Exercise is a great way to release tension and boost mood. It promotes the production of endorphins, which are natural mood enhancers. Even a simple walk or stretching session can have a positive impact on stress levels.
  3. Prioritize self-care activities that promote relaxation and rejuvenation: It is important to carve out time for activities that bring joy and relaxation. This could include hobbies, reading, taking baths, listening to music, or spending time in nature. Self-care activities help to recharge and replenish our energy levels.
  4. Seek social support from friends, family, or support groups: Connecting with loved ones and having a strong support network can help to alleviate stress. Talking to someone about your feelings or concerns can provide relief and perspective. Joining support groups or engaging in social activities can also foster a sense of belonging and reduce feelings of isolation.
  5. Set realistic goals and manage time effectively: Feeling overwhelmed can contribute to stress. Setting realistic goals and breaking tasks into smaller, manageable steps can make them feel more achievable. Effective time management techniques, such as creating schedules or to-do lists, can help prioritize tasks and reduce stress associated with time pressures.
  6. Learn to say no and set boundaries to avoid becoming overwhelmed: It is important to set boundaries and prioritize your own well-being. Learning to say no to additional commitments or responsibilities that may overload your schedule can help prevent burnout and excessive stress.
  7. Take breaks and practice relaxation techniques during the day: Taking regular breaks throughout the day can help prevent stress from building up. Engaging in relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing or progressive muscle relaxation, during these breaks can help to reset and refocus the mind.
  8. Identify and challenge negative thoughts or beliefs that contribute to stress: Negative thinking patterns can fuel stress and anxiety. Becoming aware of negative thoughts and actively challenging them with more realistic and positive perspectives can help reduce stress levels. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) techniques can be helpful for identifying and modifying negative thinking patterns.
  9. Seek professional help from a psychologist or therapist if necessary: If stress becomes overwhelming and begins to significantly impact daily functioning, seeking professional help from a psychologist or therapist can be beneficial. They can provide guidance, support, and evidence-based strategies to better manage stress and improve overall well-being.

Stress is a natural part of life, and in small amounts, it can even be beneficial. However, prolonged periods of stress can have detrimental effects on our physical and mental well-being. It is important to be aware of the symptoms of harmful stress and take proactive steps to alleviate it in our busy lives.

By incorporating stress-management techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, and mindfulness into our daily routines, we can learn to calm our minds and promote relaxation. Engaging in regular physical activity or exercise helps release tension and boost mood. Prioritizing self-care activities that bring joy and relaxation allows us to recharge and rejuvenate.

Seeking social support from friends, family, or support groups ensures that we have a strong support network to turn to during stressful times. Setting realistic goals and managing time effectively helps prevent feelings of overwhelm. It is also important to learn to say no and set boundaries to avoid becoming overloaded.

Taking regular breaks throughout the day and practicing relaxation techniques during these breaks can help prevent stress from building up. Identifying and challenging negative thoughts or beliefs that contribute to stress can lead to a more positive and resilient mindset. And if stress becomes overwhelming, seeking professional help from a psychologist or therapist can provide valuable guidance and support.

By implementing these strategies, we can navigate back to a sense of peace and well-being, reducing the impact of stress on our lives. Remember, taking care of our mental and emotional health is crucial, and prioritizing self-care is not selfish - it is essential for leading a balanced and fulfilling life.

title: Recognising Depression at Work and Taking Action
excerpt: Depression can affect anyone, anywhere, and it is not uncommon for it to manifest in the workplace. If you suspect that you might be struggling with depression at work, it's...
content:
Depression can affect anyone, anywhere, and it is not uncommon for it to manifest in the workplace.

If you suspect that you might be struggling with depression at work, it's crucial to recognise the symptoms and take proactive steps to address it.

Remember, you're not alone, and there is support available to help you navigate through this challenging time.

Recognising the Symptoms

Depression can manifest in various ways, and it's important to be aware of the common signs that may indicate you are experiencing depression at work. These symptoms can include conflict, isolation, indecision, loss of interest, procrastination, lack of motivation, poor communication, difficulty concentrating, and frequently calling in sick. If you find yourself experiencing several of these symptoms, it's essential to acknowledge that you may be dealing with depression.

Differentiating Depression from Burnout

It's important to understand the distinction between depression and burnout. While they share similarities, recognising the differences can help guide your approach to seeking support and addressing your mental health.

Burnout typically occurs when you feel overwhelmed by prolonged stress and exhaustion, while depression may stem from untreated anxiety, depression, and fear. By understanding this, you can better determine the appropriate course of action.

Taking Action Seeking Support and Help

1. Reach out to a mental health professional or Doctor

Seeking professional help is crucial in managing workplace depression. Schedule an appointment with a mental health professional or your doctor to discuss your symptoms honestly. They can provide a proper diagnosis and recommend a treatment plan, which may involve therapy, medication, and self-reflection.

2. Communicate with your support system

Don't underestimate the power of sharing your struggles with your support system. Open up to your family, friends, or colleagues about what you're going through. Their understanding and support can help alleviate feelings of isolation and provide a network of assistance.

3. Utilise available resources

Check if your employer offers an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) that provides support, counselling, and resources for employees facing personal or work-related challenges. Additionally, there are helplines, support groups, and mental health apps available that can offer assistance. Don't hesitate to utilise these resources, even if you don't have insurance.

4. Communicate your needs

Be open with your supervisor and colleagues about your limitations and needs. If you're struggling to meet deadlines or need additional support, express your concerns and ask for accommodations. Remember, your mental health should be a priority, and it's okay to ask for help.

5. Make lifestyle changes

Addressing your overall well-being can have a positive impact on managing depression. Focus on adopting healthy eating habits, incorporating exercise into your routine, getting enough sleep, and reducing stressors in your life. Small changes in your lifestyle can make a significant difference in managing your mental health.

Recognising and managing depression at work is essential for your overall well-being and productivity.

By being aware of the symptoms, seeking professional help, and utilising available resources, you can take proactive steps towards addressing your mental health. Remember, you are not alone, and there is support available to guide you through this challenging journey.

Prioritise your well-being, communicate your needs, and make positive lifestyle changes to take control of your depression and create a healthier work environment for yourself.

title: Navigating Mental Health Support in Australia
excerpt: The Mental Health Treatment Plan Explained Mental health is an important aspect of overall well-being, and it's crucial to seek support when needed. In Australia, there is a...
content:
The Mental Health Treatment Plan Explained

Mental health is an important aspect of overall well-being, and it's crucial to seek support when needed. In Australia, there is a system in place called the Mental Health Treatment Plan, which provides individuals with access to free or subsidized sessions with qualified mental health professionals.

Understanding the Mental Health Treatment Plan

Previously known as the Mental Health Care Plan, the Mental Health Treatment Plan is available to anyone in Australia who requires support for a mental health condition. This plan is a part of the Medicare system and allows individuals to receive free or subsidized sessions from registered or clinical psychologists, eligible social workers, and occupational therapists.

Visiting Your GP To begin the process, you'll need to visit your General Practitioner (GP). Your GP will help you identify how you've been feeling and determine the best type of support for you.

They may create a Mental Health Treatment Plan for you and refer you to an eligible mental health professional. With this plan, you can access up to 10 free or subsidized sessions per year.

It's important to note that you can't have all 10 sessions at once. After your initial six sessions, you will need to revisit your GP for a Mental Health Treatment Plan review. During this review, you and your GP will collaboratively decide if you require further sessions.

How the Plan Can Help You, aside from providing access to free or subsidized mental health care, the Mental Health Treatment Plan is an excellent starting point towards improving your mental well-being.

This plan can help you feel more in control of your mental health, gain clarity and insight into your feelings, feel connected and supported, and break down big challenges into manageable steps.

Getting Started with the Plan, after obtaining a Mental Health Treatment Plan might seem daunting at first, but your GP will guide you through the process. During your appointment, it's essential to communicate openly with your GP about your mental health and your intention to get a plan.

Your GP will need to make a mental health diagnosis, but rest assured, it's confidential and only meant to ensure you receive the necessary support.

Once your GP determines that a Mental Health Treatment Plan is appropriate for you, they will typically recommend a nearby service or mental health professional. If you have a specific preference, feel free to share it with your GP.

You don't need to make a decision on the spot; take your time to review your options before contacting your GP to finalize your choice.

Maximizing Your time when visiting the GP, when you are considering booking an appointment with a GP find one who has an interest in mental health. Prepare any questions you may have about the process, the type of mental health professional suitable for you, and what a diagnosis means for your treatment. It's also crucial to allocate time both before and after your appointment to mentally prepare and decompress.

Taking care of your mental health is essential, and the Mental Health Treatment Plan in Australia offers valuable support. By visiting your GP and creating a plan, you can access free or subsidized sessions with qualified mental health professionals. Remember, you are not alone, and seeking help is an important step towards feeling better. Reach out to your GP today and embark on your journey towards improved mental well-being.

More information can be found on the Services Australia web site - Mental Health Care and Medicare

Immediate danger or in crisis and need support

If anyone’s life is in immediate danger, call 000 or visit a hospital emergency department.

If you’re in crisis and need support, call Lifeline on 13 11 14. They’re open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

title: Understanding Stress and Anxiety
excerpt: In today's fast-paced and demanding world, stress and anxiety have become all too common. The pressures of work, personal relationships, financial concerns, and global events can...
content:
In today's fast-paced and demanding world, stress and anxiety have become all too common.
The pressures of work, personal relationships, financial concerns, and global events can take a toll on our mental health, we will explore the intricacies of stress and anxiety, their impact on our well-being, and effective strategies to manage and alleviate these conditions.
By gaining a deeper understanding of stress and anxiety, we can empower ourselves to lead happier, more balanced lives.

What is Stress?

  1. Stress is a natural response triggered by various external or internal factors. It is the body's way of preparing itself for potential threats or challenges.
  2. Types of Stress:
    a) Acute Stress, Brief and intense stress response, often in response to immediate circumstances.
    b) Chronic Stress, Prolonged stress that persists over an extended period, leading to severe physical and mental health consequences.
  3. Causes and Symptoms of Stress:
    a) Common stressors, Workload, personal relationships, financial difficulties, major life changes.
    b) Physical symptoms, Headaches, muscle tension, fatigue, sleep disturbances.
    c) Psychological symptoms, Irritability, difficulty concentrating, racing thoughts.
    d) Understanding Anxiety
    Anxiety is a persistent state of unease or fear that may not necessarily have an identifiable cause.
    It involves excessive worry and apprehension about future events or perceived threats.
    Types of Anxiety Disorders:
  4. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), Chronic and excessive worry about various aspects of life.
    a) Panic Disorder, Recurrent panic attacks characterized by sudden and intense fear.
    b) Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD), Fear of social situations and judgment from others.
    c) Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Anxiety triggered by past traumatic experiences.
  5. Causes and Symptoms of Anxiety
    a) Genetic and environmental factors.
    b) Traumatic experiences, childhood upbringing, or imbalanced brain chemistry.
    c) Symptoms: Restlessness, panic attacks, difficulty breathing, excessive sweating.

The Impact of Stress and Anxiety on Mental Health

  1. Relationship between Stress and Anxiety
    a) While stress is a natural response, chronic stress can contribute to the development of anxiety disorders.
    b) Increased stress levels often heighten anxiety symptoms, creating a vicious cycle.
  2. Long-term Consequences of Stress and Anxiety:
    a) Mental health implications, Depression, increased risk of substance abuse, decreased overall well-being.
    b) Physical health implications, Cardiovascular issues, weakened immune system, gastrointestinal problems.

Effective Strategies for Managing Stress and Anxiety

  1. Self-Care Techniques
    a) Prioritizing sleep and establishing a calming bedtime routine.
    b) Regular exercise and physical activity to release tension and boost endorphins.
    c) Practicing relaxation techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, or yoga.
  2. Cognitive-Behavioural Techniques
    a) Identifying and challenging negative thoughts and cognitive distortions.
    b) Implementing stress management techniques like time management and prioritization.
    c) Seeking professional therapy or counseling to address underlying issues.
  3. Lifestyle Modifications
    a) Maintaining a healthy and balanced diet to support overall well-being.
    b) Limiting exposure to stressors, setting boundaries, and practicing assertiveness.
    c) Engaging in hobbies and activities that bring joy and relaxation.
  4. Social Support and Connection
    a) Cultivating strong support systems through nurturing relationships with friends and family.
    b) Joining support groups or seeking peer support to share experiences and coping strategies
    c) Engaging in open communication and seeking help when needed.
    Stress and anxiety are part of our lives, but managing them effectively is crucial for our mental and physical well-being.

By understanding the triggers and symptoms of stress and anxiety, we can develop personalized strategies to mitigate their impact.
Through self-care practices, cognitive-behavioural techniques, lifestyle modifications, and seeking support, we can regain control over our mental health.
Remember, seeking professional help when needed is a sign of strength and can provide valuable guidance on the journey towards better mental well-being.

title: The Journey We Take on ANZAC Day
excerpt: Anzac Day holds a significant place in the hearts of Australians and New Zealanders as a day of remembrance and reflection. It commemorates the courage and sacrifice of those who...
content:
Anzac Day holds a significant place in the hearts of Australians and New Zealanders as a day of remembrance and reflection. It commemorates the courage and sacrifice of those who fought in the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps (ANZAC) during World War I. However, in recent times, society has been gradually disconnecting itself from the true essence and meaning of this solemn day. Anzac Day is not merely a public holiday or an opportunity for a long weekend getaway.

It is a day that aims to honor the bravery, resilience, and sacrifice of our servicemen and women who

fought for our freedom. It serves as a reminder of the realities of war and its profound impact on individuals, families, and communities. Anzac Day also fosters a sense of national identity and unity, as we collectively reflect on the sacrifices made by our ancestors. Over the years, Anzac Day has evolved beyond its original focus on World War I. It now encompasses recognition and remembrance of all Australian and New Zealand servicemen and women who have served in conflicts and peacekeeping operations. This expansion of scope widens the understanding and commemoration of the sacrifices made across generations.

In recent times, society's engagement with the true meaning of Anzac Day has been diminishing. With each passing year, fewer people attend dawn services or actively participate in commemorative events. This disconnection is partly attributed to the fading memories of World War I and the subsequent conflicts. However, another significant factor is society's growing detachment from the harsh realities of war. The majority of us have never experienced the horrors of battle or witnessed the toll it takes on individuals' or the families mental and physical well-being.

The rise of social media has further contributed to society's dissociation from the real issues of war. While platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter have facilitated the sharing of Anzac Day commemorations and stories, they have also diluted the depth of understanding and empathy. Quick likes, shares, and one-line comments often replace thoughtful reflection or genuine engagement. This superficial connection to the day's significance can lead to a lack of awareness about the long-lasting effects of war, such as depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), experienced by veterans and their families. Long are the days of waking before dawn to get yourself and the family down to the dawn service to stand with your community and listen to the spin chilling Last Post as a lone soldier play the bugle call to end the days activities and to pay tribute to fallen soldiers, coming home to watch the parades on the tv or better heading to watch the parade.

Anzac Day holds a special place in our hearts as a moment to remember and honor the sacrifices made by our servicemen and women. However, society's disconnection from the true realities of war threatens the integrity and purpose of this solemn day. It is crucial to reestablish a genuine understanding and appreciation for the physical, emotional, and mental toll that war takes on individuals. By actively engaging with the stories and experiences of veterans, we can ensure that Anzac Day continues to serve its purpose as a day of remembrance and reflection.

It is important to reestablish a genuine understanding and appreciation for the physical, emotional, and mental toll that war takes on individuals by actively engaging with the stories and experiences of veterans.

title: Understanding Suicide Bereavement
excerpt: Statement We recognise that discussing suicide and suicide bereavement is not an easy subject and can evoke intense emotions. If you or someone you know is struggling with...
content:
Statement

We recognise that discussing suicide and suicide bereavement is not an easy subject and can evoke intense emotions.

If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide or is in need of support, please reach out to helpline services such as

  • Lifeline
  • Beyond Blue

Link to these services contact information here

These organizations provide confidential and compassionate assistance from trained professionals who can offer guidance and a listening ear in times of crisis. Remember, seeking help is a sign of strength, and there are people ready to support you through your journey of healing and resilience.

Navigating the Storm of Loss and Healing

Losing a loved one to suicide is a devastating and life-altering experience.

The survivors, referred to as suicide bereaved, are left to navigate a complex web of emotions, including profound grief, feelings of being lost, anger, and frustration.

As we will delve into the unique journey of suicide bereavement, exploring the raw emotions experienced by those left behind and shedding light on the available support from mental health practitioners.

By understanding the depth of these experiences and the resources available, we can foster healing and resilience for those affected by suicide.

The Turmoil of Suicide Bereavement

Grief

Suicide bereavement elicits an intense and multifaceted grief response, encompassing sadness, despair, and a deep longing for the deceased loved one. The sudden loss and traumatic nature of suicide amplify these emotions.

Grief triggers physical, emotional, and cognitive responses, impacting sleep patterns, appetite, and the ability to concentrate. Understanding the various stages of grief can help survivors navigate their journey.

Feeling Lost

Suicide often leaves survivors feeling adrift, as if their sense of purpose and direction has been shattered. The unexpected nature of the death and unanswered questions contribute to a profound sense of confusion and disorientation.

It is vital for suicide bereaved to seek support and guidance in rediscovering their identity and finding a new sense of purpose amidst the pain and loss.

The Weight of Guilt, Anger, and Frustration

Guilt: Suicide bereaved frequently grapple with guilt, blaming themselves for not recognizing the signs or preventing the tragedy. It is crucial to emphasize that suicide is a complex issue, and individuals cannot solely shoulder the blame.

Anger and Frustration: Survivors may experience intense anger towards the deceased, themselves, or others, as they struggle to make sense of the unimaginable loss. Finding healthy ways to express and process these emotions is essential for healing.

The Stigma Surrounding Suicide

The social stigma associated with suicide adds an additional layer of pain and isolation for the bereaved. Society's misconceptions and judgments can exacerbate feelings of shame and prevent open discussions about mental health and suicide.

Challenging and breaking down the stigma surrounding suicide is crucial for creating a supportive environment for suicide bereaved individuals.

Mental Health Practitioners' Guidance for Healing

Therapy and Counselling

Mental health practitioners, specializing in suicide bereavement, provide a safe space for survivors to express their grief, confusion, anger, and other complex emotions.

Therapeutic interventions, such as individual or group counselling, can help survivors navigate the healing process.

Various therapeutic approaches, including cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT), acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and narrative therapy, can aid in processing grief and rebuilding a sense of self.

Grief Education

Mental health practitioners educate survivors about the normal and complex aspects of grief after suicide.

By understanding the unique challenges, survivors can find solace in knowing that their emotions and reactions are valid and shared by others.

Grief education also encompasses providing information about the physical and psychological effects of grief, coping strategies, and self-care techniques to promote resilience.

Support Groups and Community

Suicide bereavement support groups offer a safe and compassionate environment for survivors to connect with others who have experienced similar loss.

These groups like the Wandering Man provide a sense of community, understanding, and validation, helping survivors feel less alone in their journey.

Online resources and forums provide access to educational materials, support networks, and mental health professionals specializing in suicide bereavement. These resources are particularly valuable for those in remote areas or who prefer online support.

Advocacy and Education

Mental health practitioners play a crucial role in challenging the stigma surrounding suicide and mental health.

By conducting community outreach programs, delivering educational workshops, and advocating for more resources, they strive to create a more compassionate and supportive society.

Collaboration with other professionals, such as medical practitioners, psychiatrists, and social workers, ensures comprehensive care and support for the bereaved.

The aftermath of losing a loved one to suicide is an arduous journey, marked by profound grief, disorientation, anger, and frustration.

However, it is essential to remember that healing and support are available. Mental health practitioners specialise in providing guidance, understanding, and resources to navigate the complex emotions experienced by suicide bereaved.

By fostering open conversations, challenging stigma, and promoting education, we can create a society that embraces and supports those affected by suicide.

Together, let us extend a helping hand to those in need, providing the compassion and empathy required during their journey of healing and resilience.

title: The Hidden Struggles of Loneliness and Depression in Society
excerpt: In today's fast-paced world, where we are more connected than ever through technology, it may seem paradoxical that loneliness and depression are prevalent issues in our society....
content:
In today's fast-paced world, where we are more connected than ever through technology, it may seem paradoxical that loneliness and depression are prevalent issues in our society. However, the truth is that these silent battles affect individuals across various age groups and backgrounds. In this blog, we will delve into the impact of loneliness and depression on individuals and provide examples of how these challenges manifest in our society.

Loneliness is our society is a Silent Epidemic

Loneliness can be described as a subjective feeling of isolation or disconnection from others, even when surrounded by people. It is important to note that loneliness is not solely determined by the number of social connections one has but rather the quality and depth of those connections.

One group of individuals particularly susceptible to loneliness is the elderly. Many older adults may experience loneliness due to factors such as retirement, loss of loved ones, or limited social interactions. The absence of meaningful connections can lead to feelings of isolation and vulnerability. Imagine an elderly person who has recently retired, losing the daily social interactions that came with their job. They may struggle to find new ways to connect with others and feel a deep sense of loneliness as a result.

Interestingly, even young adults in the digital age can experience loneliness. Paradoxically, while social media platforms have made it easier to connect with others, they can also contribute to loneliness. Constant comparison, fear of missing out, and the pressure to present a perfect life online can lead to feelings of inadequacy and isolation. Picture a young adult scrolling through their social media feed, seeing their friends posting pictures of parties and gatherings they were not invited to. This constant exposure to social activities they feel excluded from can intensify their feelings of loneliness.

Another group that often grapples with loneliness is single parents. Balancing the responsibilities of parenthood without a partner can be emotionally challenging. Single parents may experience loneliness due to the lack of adult companionship and the absence of a support system. Imagine a single parent who works long hours to provide for their child, with little time for socializing or building new relationships. They may yearn for adult companionship and feel a deep sense of loneliness despite being surrounded by their child's love.

Depression can lead to withdrawing and put The Weight of Emotional Desolation on our shoulders.

Depression is a mental health disorder characterized by persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and a loss of interest in activities once enjoyed. It can significantly impact an individual's daily functioning and overall well-being.

One example of depression in society is the pressure faced by students to excel academically. The competitive nature of education systems and the fear of failure can take a toll on students, leading to feelings of overwhelm, self-doubt, and a sense of hopelessness. Imagine a student who constantly compares themselves to their high-achieving peers, feeling inadequate and unable to meet the unrealistic expectations placed upon them. This constant pressure can contribute to the development of depression.

Postpartum depression is another example of depression in society. New mothers may experience a range of emotions after childbirth, including postpartum depression. This condition, often accompanied by feelings of sadness, exhaustion, and a sense of inadequacy, can affect the mother-infant bond and overall family dynamics. Imagine a new mother who feels overwhelmed by the responsibilities of caring for a newborn, experiencing sleep deprivation and feelings of guilt for not being able to enjoy motherhood as she expected. These overwhelming emotions can lead to postpartum depression, making it difficult for her to bond with her baby and exacerbating her feelings of despair.

Workplace stress is yet another factor that can contribute to depression in society. The modern work environment can be demanding, with long hours, high expectations, and a competitive atmosphere. Chronic workplace stress can take a toll on an individual's mental health, leading to decreased productivity, increased absence, and strained relationships. Imagine an employee who faces constant pressure to meet tight deadlines, work overtime, and maintain a high level of performance. Over time, this chronic stress can lead to feelings of burnout and depression, impacting not only their work but also their personal life. Loneliness and depression are not to be underestimated. They can affect anyone, regardless of age, background, or social status. It is crucial to recognize the signs and symptoms of these challenges and offer support and understanding to those who may be struggling. By raising awareness, fostering meaningful connections, and promoting mental health initiatives, we can work towards a society that embraces empathy, compassion, and a sense of belonging for all. Let us strive to create a world where no one feels alone in their battles with loneliness and depression.

This month, we’re honored to welcome our special guest speaker, Damian Bourke, who will share his incredible story of resilience and strength.
We’re also excited to have Charlie Bezzina, our renowned speaker from April, joining us once again - it’s a great opportunity to hear from him.
Whether you’re a first-timer or a familiar face, this is a unique chance to connect, share stories, and draw courage from the powerful journeys of Damian and Charlie.

💡 Event Highlights:
• Speaker of the Month: Damian Bourke
• A good opportunity to hear from Charlie Bezzina again
• An open and inclusive space for all
• Female supporters are warmly welcome
• A dedicated kids’ zone to keep the little ones entertained

🗓️ Date: This Sunday - 24th Nov
⏰ Time: 1PM - 4PM
📍 Location: 4-32 Province Blvd, Highton VIC 3216

Let’s come together for an afternoon filled with inspiration, community, and courage. We can’t wait to see you there! 💙

We’re looking for enthusiastic helpers to lend a hand to setup the venue. Whether you're a pro or just love being part of the action, your contribution will make a big difference. If you’re available to help, please let us know

We are truly grateful to everyone who joined us on Sunday, November 24th, making the event such a remarkable success.
With over 50 attendees, the day was filled with meaningful connections, inspiring moments, and a strong sense of community - all thanks to your support.
A heartfelt thank you to our guest speaker, Damian Bourke, for sharing his valuable insights, and to our past speakers - Charlie Bezzina, Steve Hall (The Game Changer), and Mark Smith - whose ongoing contributions continue to inspire and uplift us.
We were also delighted to have Gorge from Chill Breathe Revive join us and add his expertise to the gathering.
To our dedicated volunteers - your hard work in cooking the BBQ, setting up, and packing up the venue did not go unnoticed.
A special thank you to our BBQ sponsors, Grovedale Meats and Hi Lite Amusements, for your generous support in making the day extra special.
We also extend our gratitude to the wonderful women who joined us and offered their encouragement - it means so much. And to OneHope Baptist Church - Barrabool Hills Campus, thank you for providing us with a fantastic venue and a supervised kids' play zone, which was a hit with families. Your support is invaluable.
We cannot express our gratitude enough to every single one of you. This gathering wouldn’t have been possible without your contributions, and we are so blessed to have shared this experience together.

**Mark Your Calendars!**
Our next event, Orphan Christmas Day, will be held on December 25th. Don’t forget to like our Facebook page to stay updated, and we hope to see you there!

Thank you all once again for making this event so special. Together, we are building something truly extraordinary.
